days.title: Touchdown
days.subtitle: Saturday Apr 11 · Arrival from Toronto via Narita · Evening only
days.note: Flight AC009 lands Narita T1 at 15:50. Budget ~90 min for immigration + Narita Express/Skyliner to Ueno. You'll be jetlagged — keep this evening light.

events.title: Arrive Narita T1 · Flight AC009
events.tagline: 13h 20m from Toronto YYZ T1 · Departed 13:30 prev day
events.notes: Clear immigration, pick up luggage, grab a Suica card at the airport convenience store or machines. Take Narita Express or Skyliner to Ueno (~60 min).

events.title: Narita Express → Ueno
events.notes: Narita Express runs every 30 min to Tokyo/Ueno stations. Can also take Keisei Skyliner directly to Ueno (36 min, ¥2,520).

events.title: Check in · Tosei Hotel Cocone Ueno
Explore Ameyoko Market area
events.tagline: Street food and evening energy near Ueno Station
events.notes: Ameyoko is a bustling open-air market right outside Ueno Station. Great for a casual first dinner — yakitori, takoyaki, fresh seafood. Many stalls open until 8–9pm.

days.title: Tokyo to Kanazawa
days.subtitle: Sunday Apr 12 · Travel day · ~4.5 hours by train
days.note: Train booked: 9:26 AM from Ueno Station. Hokuriku Shinkansen to Kanazawa. Arrive around 2pm — half-day to explore.

accommodation.name: Four Points Flex by Sheraton Kanazawa

events.title: Hokuriku Shinkansen · Ueno → Kanazawa
events.notes: Departs Ueno Station. Grab ekiben (station bento) for lunch on the train. Beautiful scenery through the Japanese Alps.

events.title: Arrive Kanazawa · Check in · Four Points Flex
events.notes: Train arrives 11:52am. Drop bags at hotel — standard check-in is 3pm but bags can be left.

events.title: Lunch · Ōmicho Market
events.tagline: 300-year-old covered market — kaisendon and market grazing
events.notes: Kanazawa faces the Sea of Japan's richest fishing grounds. Get a kaisendon (seafood rice bowl) from one of the market stalls or upstairs restaurants. ¥1,500–2,500. Go before 2pm for best selection. Also try the gold-leaf soft cream.

events.title: Nagamachi Samurai District
events.notes: Wander the canal-side earthen wall lanes — the narrow stone path with water on one side is the defining photo of Kanazawa. Visit Nomura-ke residence (¥550) for tatami rooms, a small garden, and Edo-period artefacts. Best before crowds pick up — quiet on a Sunday afternoon.

events.title: Higashi Chaya District at dusk
events.tagline: Lanterns glow on wooden lattice teahouses
events.notes: Walk the main street as lanterns come on — crowds thin after 5:30pm and the warm light on wooden facades is beautiful. Cross the Asanogawa River to Kazuemachi for 15 min: quieter lanes, stone steps, best river views of the district at dusk.

events.title: Dinner · Higashi Chaya / Kazuemachi area
events.tagline: Evening meal after a light arrival day
events.notes: Several izakayas and traditional restaurants in the Higashi Chaya area. Look for jibuni stew (Kanazawa's signature duck and fu stew in dashi) or Kanazawa oden for something local and warming.

days.title: Gardens, museums & ninja temple
days.subtitle: Monday Apr 13 · Full day · Out by 8am
days.note: A full day anchored by Kenrokuen in the morning and Myoryuji Ninja Temple in the afternoon (reservation dependent). Museums fill the midday. Relaxed pace — take time in the garden.

accommodation.name: Four Points Flex by Sheraton Kanazawa

events.title: Kenrokuen Garden
events.tagline: One of Japan's three great gardens — photography focus
events.notes: ¥320 entry (paid hours begin 7am). Priority shots: Kotoji Lantern reflected in Kasumigaike pond, the Yūgao-tei teahouse (1774), and the cherry trees along the northeast streams — should still be beautiful mid-April. Take your time. Weekday mornings are quiet.

events.title: Kanazawa Castle Park
events.tagline: Adjacent to Kenrokuen — outdoor grounds and moat
events.notes: Walk straight in from Kenrokuen — they share a border. Keep it brief: focus on the outdoor grounds, the white castle walls, and moat-side photo angles. Skip the interior buildings (reconstructed). Free to walk.

events.title: Seisonkaku Villa
events.tagline: The Maeda lord's private palace — lacquerware, Dutch glass, tatami
events.notes: Right at the Kenrokuen gate, zero travel time. Built 1863 as a retirement villa for the lord's mother — Dutch stained-glass windows, lacquerware sliding screens, and painted ceilings. A fusion of Japanese and Western aesthetics almost no tourists go inside to see. ¥700.

events.title: Coffee · Kanazawaya
events.notes: Confirm location and route to D.T. Suzuki Museum from here.

events.title: D.T. Suzuki Museum
events.tagline: Zen philosopher's contemplative museum — Water Mirror Garden
events.notes: ¥310. Designed by Yoshio Taniguchi (who also redesigned MoMA). The centrepiece Water Mirror Garden is a perfectly still reflecting pool — one of the most photogenic spaces in Kanazawa and almost always quiet. Visit on a clear morning for mirror-like reflections.

events.title: Sit-down lunch
events.notes: Route lunch toward Teramachi/south if Ninja Temple is booked for the afternoon. Options: jibuni stew at a traditional restaurant, Kanazawa curry (local institution, ¥800–1,000), or a kaiseki-lite set lunch. Avoid another seafood bowl if you had kaisendon yesterday.

events.title: Myoryuji — Ninja Temple
events.notes: Reservation dependent — call today to book an afternoon slot. ¥1,200 adults, cash only. 40-min guided tour in Japanese with English booklet. No photography inside. Located in Teramachi district, south of the city — take the Loop Bus (Left Loop, Hirokoji stop, ~14 min from Station). Nishi Chaya district is a 3-min walk away — combine the two.

events.title: Nishi Chaya District
events.tagline: Smallest, quietest geisha district — almost no tourists
events.notes: 3-minute walk from Myoryuji. Wooden lattice teahouses from 200 years ago, stone-paved street. On quiet afternoons you can sometimes hear shamisen from upper floors. Free to walk.

events.title: Dinner · Evening
events.notes: Consider Kanazawa oden (delicate kombu broth, premium local ingredients — a classic Kanazawa evening dish) or a nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) focused restaurant. Much cheaper here than in Tokyo or Osaka for the same fish.

days.title: Shirakawa-go day trip
days.subtitle: Tuesday Apr 14 · Day trip · UNESCO thatched village
days.note: Shirakawa-go is a UNESCO World Heritage village of steep thatched-roof farmhouses (gassho-zukuri). Bus from Kanazawa takes ~75 min each way. Book bus tickets in advance — Nohi Bus or Hokutetsu. Recommended to book online before the trip.

accommodation.name: Four Points Flex by Sheraton Kanazawa

events.title: Bus · Kanazawa → Shirakawa-go
events.tagline: Nohi Bus from Kanazawa Station East Exit
events.notes: Book in advance online. ~¥2,600 each way (~$25 CAD). Reserved seating. Several departures daily — 8am gets you there before tour buses arrive.

events.title: Shirakawa-go village walk
events.tagline: Thatched gassho-zukuri farmhouses and rice paddies
events.notes: Explore the main Ogimachi village on foot. Visit Wada House or Kanda House — open farmhouse museums showing life inside the massive thatched structures. The village is compact and walkable in 2 hours at a relaxed pace.

events.title: Shiroyama Viewpoint
events.notes: 15-min uphill walk from the village centre (or short shuttle bus). The postcard shot of the entire village with mountains behind. Best light is morning — you'll be hitting it at the right time. Go before the tour buses arrive in force around 11am.

events.title: Lunch in Shirakawa-go
events.tagline: Eat before the tour-bus lunch rush
events.notes: Several small restaurants serve local specialties. Try hida beef croquettes, handmade soba, or mitarashi dango. Eat by noon — tour groups flood restaurants from 12:30 onwards.

events.title: Bus · Shirakawa-go → Kanazawa
events.notes: Check return bus times when booking — aim for a 2–3pm departure to give yourselves a relaxed evening back in Kanazawa.

events.title: Free evening · Last night in Kanazawa
events.notes: Katamachi is Kanazawa's main entertainment and bar district near the Sai River — good for a final evening drink. Or revisit Higashi Chaya if you want more time there.

days.title: Arrival & first impressions
days.subtitle: Wednesday Apr 15 · Travel day from Kanazawa · Afternoon / evening only
days.note: Kanazawa → Kyoto is ~2.5 hrs by Thunderbird limited express. Train Voucher Booked via Klook — redeem at ticket machine at station. Arrive Kyoto Station by early afternoon.

events.title: Thunderbird · Kanazawa → Kyoto
events.tagline: Klook voucher — redeem at ticket machine
events.notes: Redeem Klook voucher at JR West ticket machine before boarding. Reserved seating.

events.title: Check in · Hotel Grand Bach
events.tagline: Drop bags, freshen up, get oriented
events.notes: Hotel is in the Kawaramachi / Gion area — perfectly positioned for evening walks.

events.title: Nishiki Market
events.notes: A 5-block covered arcade packed with pickles, fresh tofu, tamagoyaki, yakitori, and sweets. Perfect first stop — low-pressure grazing for a late lunch. Most stalls open until 6pm.

events.title: Hanamikoji Street at dusk
events.tagline: Best light of the day on the lantern lanes
events.notes: The famous lantern-lit Gion street is most photogenic between sunset and full dark. Walk slowly south from Shijo-dori. Maiko sightings are most likely between 5:30–7pm.

events.title: Dinner · Pontocho Alley
events.tagline: Pick a counter seat in the lantern lane
events.notes: Narrow alley one block west of the Kamo River. Mix of budget yakitori counters, izakayas, and higher-end kaiseki. Look for kawayuka riverside platforms (seasonal Apr–Sept).

days.title: Eastern hills & mountain temple
days.subtitle: Thursday Apr 16 · Full day · Early morning start · ~18,000 steps
days.note: Highest-effort day — wear good shoes. Morning in the eastern hills, afternoon escape to Kurama for the mountain hike to Kibune.

events.title: Kiyomizudera Temple
events.notes: The iconic wooden stage temple built into the hillside. With eastern morning light and almost no one else there, it's one of the best photo moments in Japan. ¥500 entry.

events.title: Ninen-zaka & Sannen-zaka lanes
events.tagline: Stone-paved lanes, empty in early morning
events.notes: Walk down from Kiyomizudera through these beautifully preserved machiya lanes. Before 9am they're virtually empty.

events.title: Sanjusangendo
events.notes: A long hall containing 1,001 life-size statues of the thousand-armed Kannon. One of Japan's most awe-inspiring interiors. ¥600 entry. No photography inside.

events.title: Kurama-dera Temple hike
events.tagline: Mountain temple + hike through to Kibune
events.notes: Take the Eizan Railway to Kurama Station (~30 min from Demachiyanagi). Hike up to Kurama-dera temple, then over the mountain ridge and down into Kibune village. The full hike is ~90 min.

events.title: Lunch in Kibune
events.tagline: Riverside dining in the mountain village
events.notes: Kibune is famous for nagashi somen (flowing noodles) in summer and kawadoko (riverside dining platforms). Several small restaurants along the stream.

events.title: Kibuneguchi Station → Demachiyanagi
events.tagline: Eizan Railway back to central Kyoto

days.title: Western Kyoto & Gion
days.subtitle: Friday Apr 17 · Full day · Early morning start

events.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Forest
events.tagline: Go at dawn — crowds arrive by 9am
events.notes: The towering bamboo grove is magical in early morning light with no crowds. Take the JR San-in Line from Kyoto Station to Saga-Arashiyama Station (~15 min).

events.title: Okochi Sanso Garden
events.tagline: Hilltop villa with views over Kyoto
events.notes: A beautiful hilltop garden estate at the end of the bamboo path. Entry includes matcha and a sweet on the terrace with panoramic views. ¥1,000.

events.title: Fushimi Inari Taisha
events.notes: The famous tunnel of orange torii gates up Mt. Inari. The full hike to the summit takes ~2 hours round trip, but even 30 min up is spectacular. Free entry.

events.title: Tea Ceremony
events.notes: Pre-booked tea ceremony experience. Dress respectfully.

events.title: Hanamikoji + Gion evening wander
events.tagline: Last evening in Kyoto's most atmospheric streets
events.notes: Revisit Hanamikoji at dusk and explore the wider Gion area. Look for small alley izakayas for dinner.

days.title: Kyoto to Osaka
days.subtitle: Saturday Apr 18 · Travel day · JR Special Rapid
days.note: Buy ticket at station — JR Special Rapid from Kyoto to Osaka Station (~30 min, covered by JR pass or ~¥570).

events.title: JR Special Rapid · Kyoto → Osaka
events.notes: Quick and frequent JR Special Rapid service. No reservation needed — just tap your IC card.

events.title: Check in · Hotel Monterey Grasmere
events.notes: Hotel is in the Namba area, close to Dotonbori and Shinsaibashi.

events.title: Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi
events.notes: The famous canal-side strip with giant crab signs, running man, and wall-to-wall street food. Try takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and kushikatsu.

events.title: Osaka Castle Park
events.notes: The castle exterior is photogenic (reconstruction). The park grounds are pleasant for an afternoon walk. Castle museum entry ¥600.

days.title: Osaka exploring
days.subtitle: Sunday Apr 19 · Full day · Kobe beef dinner

events.title: Shinsekai district
events.notes: Colourful retro district around Tsutenkaku Tower. Famous for kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers). Great for morning street photography.

events.title: Kuromon Market
events.tagline: Osaka's kitchen — fresh seafood and street food
events.notes: A covered market with stalls selling fresh sashimi, grilled seafood, tamagoyaki, and fruits. Eat your way through for lunch.

events.title: Free afternoon
events.tagline: Explore Amerikamura, Namba, or rest up for dinner

events.title: Kobe Beef Ishida · Osaka
events.notes: Reservation needed. High-end Kobe beef experience.

days.title: Nara day trip
days.subtitle: Monday Apr 20 · Day trip · Deer, shrines, and shopping

events.title: Train · Namba → Nara
events.tagline: Kintetsu Nara Line from Namba Station

events.title: Nara Park & Todai-ji
events.tagline: Friendly deer and the Great Buddha
events.notes: Buy deer crackers (¥200) and wander the park. Todai-ji houses the world's largest bronze Buddha in the world's largest wooden building. ¥600 entry.

events.title: Kasuga Grand Shrine
events.tagline: Most worshipped shrine in Nara — thousands of lanterns
events.notes: Famous for its hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns. The path through the forest is magical. ¥500 for inner sanctuary.

events.title: Higashimuki Shopping Street
events.tagline: Covered arcade for souvenirs and snacks
events.notes: A long covered shopping street near Kintetsu Nara Station. Good for mochi, souvenirs, and people-watching.

days.title: Kobe day trip
days.subtitle: Tuesday Apr 21 · Day trip · Port city vibes

events.title: Train · Osaka → Kobe
events.tagline: JR Special Rapid to Sannomiya Station

events.title: Kitano Ijinkan (Foreign Houses)
events.notes: Charming hilltop district with preserved European-style houses from the Meiji era. Great views over the port.

events.title: Nankinmachi (Kobe Chinatown)
events.notes: One of Japan's three Chinatowns. Compact and fun — great for pork buns, gyoza, and bubble tea.

events.title: Kobe Harborland
events.notes: Pleasant waterfront area with views of the port and Kobe Port Tower.

days.title: Osaka to Hiroshima
days.subtitle: Wednesday Apr 22 · Travel day · Shinkansen
days.note: Train Voucher Booked via Klook — redeem at JR West ticket machine before boarding.

events.title: Shinkansen · Shin-Osaka → Hiroshima
events.tagline: Klook voucher — redeem at ticket machine
events.notes: Redeem Klook voucher at JR West ticket machine before boarding. Nozomi or Sakura Shinkansen.

events.title: Peace Memorial Park & Museum
events.notes: Allow at least 2 hours for the museum. The A-Bomb Dome, Memorial Cenotaph, and Children's Peace Monument are all within the park. Museum entry ¥200.

events.title: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki
events.tagline: Layered style — noodles, cabbage, egg, everything
events.notes: Hiroshima's version uses layers instead of mixing. Try Okonomi-mura (okonomiyaki village) — a building with dozens of tiny stalls all cooking their version.

days.title: Hiroshima & Miyajima
days.subtitle: Thursday Apr 23 · Full day

events.title: Miyajima Island day trip
events.notes: Take JR to Miyajimaguchi Station (~30 min), then a short ferry to the island. The iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine is best at high tide. Check tide times! Free-roaming deer here too.

events.title: Lunch on Miyajima
events.notes: Miyajima is famous for fresh oysters and momiji manju (maple leaf cakes). The main shopping street has plenty of options.

events.title: Shukkeien Garden
events.notes: A compact but beautiful garden near the castle. ¥260 entry. Good for a peaceful late afternoon.

days.title: Hiroshima to Hakone
days.subtitle: Friday Apr 24 · Long travel day · Shinkansen + local trains
days.note: Train booked: 8:22 AM from Hiroshima. This is a long travel day — Hiroshima → Hakone-Yumoto via Shin-Osaka/Odawara. Arrive late afternoon.

accommodation.name: Yoshiike Ryokan
accommodation.notes: $1,323 · Paid · Traditional Japanese inn with onsen

events.title: Shinkansen · Hiroshima → Odawara → Hakone
events.tagline: Reserved seats booked · Transfer at Odawara
events.notes: Hiroshima → Shin-Osaka → Odawara by Shinkansen (~3.5h). Then Hakone Tozan Railway or bus to Hakone-Yumoto (~15 min). Grab ekiben for the journey.

events.title: Check in · Yoshiike Ryokan
events.notes: Yoshiike is a traditional Japanese inn with private and public onsen baths. Check in, change into the provided yukata (cotton robe), and settle in.

events.title: Explore Hakone-Yumoto town
events.tagline: Hot spring town — small shops and cafes
events.notes: Walk the main street near the station. Small souvenir shops, manju steamed buns, and foot baths along the way.

events.title: Onsen at Yoshiike
events.tagline: Soak in the hot spring baths
events.notes: Try both the indoor and outdoor (rotenburo) baths. Onsen etiquette: wash thoroughly before entering the bath. Tattoo policy varies — Yoshiike is generally tattoo-friendly.

events.title: Kaiseki dinner at ryokan
events.notes: Included with the ryokan stay. Multi-course kaiseki featuring seasonal ingredients. Served in your room or a private dining area.

days.title: Hakone full day
days.subtitle: Saturday Apr 25 · Hakone Loop · Mt. Fuji views (weather permitting)
days.note: Buy Hakone Free Pass for the loop route. Clear mornings give the best Fuji views — check the forecast!

events.title: Morning onsen + ryokan breakfast
events.tagline: Early soak, then traditional Japanese breakfast

events.title: Hakone Loop: ropeway, pirate ship, shrines
events.tagline: Cable car → Owakudani → Lake Ashi cruise
events.notes: Take the Hakone Tozan Railway up, cable car to Owakudani (volcanic valley — eat a black egg!), then ropeway down to Lake Ashi for the pirate ship cruise. Mt. Fuji views from the lake on clear days.

events.title: Hakone Shrine
events.tagline: Lakeside shrine with iconic red torii in the water
events.notes: The famous torii gate standing in Lake Ashi. Most photogenic in the morning or on overcast days when the lake is misty. Free entry.

events.title: Open-Air Museum or free time
events.notes: Hakone Open-Air Museum has sculptures set against mountain backdrop. ¥1,600 entry. Skip if tired from the loop.

days.title: Hakone to Tokyo
days.subtitle: Sunday Apr 26 · Travel day · Odakyu Romancecar
days.note: Buy Odakyu Romancecar ticket at station. Scenic express train from Hakone-Yumoto to Shinjuku (~85 min).

events.title: Odakyu Romancecar · Hakone → Shinjuku
events.notes: Reserved seat express train. Beautiful views of the Hakone mountains. Arrives at Shinjuku Station.

events.title: Settle into Tokyo area
events.tagline: Find accommodation, drop bags, get oriented
events.notes: Last stretch of the trip — 5 nights in Tokyo. Explore the neighbourhood, grab lunch.

events.title: Shinjuku or Shibuya exploring
events.tagline: Big city energy — ease back into Tokyo
events.notes: Shibuya Crossing, Shinjuku Gyoen (if cherry blossoms linger), or just wander the department stores and side streets.

days.title: Tokyo + Sushi Yoshitake
days.subtitle: Monday Apr 27 · Flex day · Mt. Fuji on best weather
days.note: This is a flexible day — if weather is clear, consider a day trip to Mt. Fuji area (Kawaguchiko). Sushi Yoshitake dinner is booked and paid ($1,156).

events.title: Flexible: Fuji day trip or Tokyo exploring
events.tagline: Check weather — go to Fuji if clear, stay in Tokyo if not
events.notes: Kawaguchiko (Mt. Fuji area) is ~2h by bus from Shinjuku. Best on crystal-clear days. If cloudy, explore Tokyo — Tsukiji outer market, Meiji Shrine, Harajuku, or Akihabara.

events.title: Sushi Yoshitake
events.notes: One of Tokyo's finest sushi experiences. Smart casual dress. Omakase only — chef's choice. Expect ~20 pieces over 2 hours. Already paid ($1,156).

days.title: Tokyo jazz night
days.subtitle: Tuesday Apr 28 · Full day · Jazz clubs in the evening

events.title: Tokyo exploring
events.tagline: Flex day — see what you missed
events.notes: Options: Teamlab Borderless, Akihabara electronics, Shimokitazawa vintage shops, Yanaka old town, or Tsukiji outer market.

events.title: Jazz clubs
events.notes:
Options:
- Pit Inn (Shinjuku) — Japan's most famous jazz club, two shows nightly
- Blue Note Tokyo (Aoyama) — international acts, upscale
- Alfie (Roppongi) — intimate, local jazz musicians

Pit Inn is the most authentic and affordable. Check schedules online.

days.title: Tokyo free day
days.subtitle: Wednesday Apr 29 · Showa Day (national holiday) · Last full day
days.note: Showa Day is a national holiday — expect some attractions to be busier than usual, but many shops and restaurants are open.

events.title: Last day in Tokyo
events.tagline: Shopping, revisiting favourites, soaking it in
events.notes: Last chance for shopping (Uniqlo Ginza, Muji, Don Quijote), revisiting favourite spots, or just wandering and soaking in the city.

events.title: Pack tonight
events.tagline: Early departure tomorrow — pack and organize bags
events.notes: Flight departs Haneda at 15:50, but plan to be at the airport by 13:00. Pack tonight so the morning is relaxed.

days.title: Departure
days.subtitle: Thursday Apr 30 · Fly home · HND → SFO → YYZ

events.title: Head to Haneda Airport
events.notes: Haneda is closer to central Tokyo than Narita. Monorail or Keikyu Line from various stations.

events.title: UA876 · Haneda (HND) T3 → San Francisco (SFO)
events.notes: International Terminal at Haneda. Crosses the date line — arrive the same calendar day.

events.title: AC740 · San Francisco (SFO) T2 → Toronto (YYZ) T1
events.notes: 2h 25m layover in SFO. Domestic terminal change may be needed.
